paper_title: Medium Bandgap Conjugated Polymer for High Performance Polymer Solar Cells Exceeding 9% Power Conversion Efficiency
source_file: /home/wzfeng/MySearch/PhotoRag/MD/Advanced Materials - 2015 - Jung - Medium Bandgap Conjugated Polymer for High Performance Polymer Solar Cells Exceeding 9 /auto/Advanced Materials - 2015 - Jung - Medium Bandgap Conjugated Polymer for High Performance Polymer Solar Cells Exceeding 9 .md

knowledge_points.content: PBDTTS-TTffBT is a donor-acceptor (D-A) copolymer composed of alkylthiothienyl-substituted benzo[1,2-b:4,5-b']dithiophene (BDTTS) as the donor, difluoro-substituted 2,1,3-benzothiadiazole (ffBT) as the acceptor, and 6-octylthieno[3,2-b]thiophene (TT) as the π bridge.
knowledge_points.evidence: we chose alkylthiothienyl substituted BDT (BDTTS) as D-unit... We also used BT or difluoro-substituted BT (ffBT) as A-unit, and utilized 6-octylthieno[3,2-b]thiophene (TT)... as π bridge unit

knowledge_points.content: The polymer solar cell based on PBDTTS-TTffBT:PC71BM achieved a maximum power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 9.44%, with an open-circuit voltage (Voc) of 0.85 V, a short-circuit current density (Jsc) of 15.43 mA/cm², and a fill factor (FF) of 0.72.
knowledge_points.evidence: The PSCs made of PBDTTS-TTffBT:PC71BM blend exhibits the best PCE of 9.44% (an average PCE of 9.22% with a Voc of 0.85 V, Jsc of 15.43 mA cm-2 and a FF of 0.72)

knowledge_points.content: Fluorine substitution on the benzothiadiazole unit in PBDTTS-TTffBT lowers the HOMO energy level to -5.45 eV (compared to -5.40 eV for the non-fluorinated PBDTTS-TTBT), which contributes to a higher open-circuit voltage (Voc) in devices.
knowledge_points.evidence: The fluorine substitution in PBDTTS-TTffBT causes deeper HOMO energy level, which may enhance Voc of the resulting PSC device... HOMO energy levels of PBDTTS-TTBT and PBDTTS-TTffBT are -5.40 and -5.45 eV, respectively

knowledge_points.content: PBDTTS-TTffBT and PBDTTS-TTBT are classified as medium bandgap polymers with optical bandgaps of 1.76 eV and 1.73 eV, respectively, and show broad light absorption from 350 to 700 nm.
knowledge_points.evidence: Two copolymers synthesized in this work exhibit medium bandgap (≈ 1.7 eV) with broad light absorption from 350 to 700 nm... we estimated the optical bandgaps of the two polymers (1.73 and 1.76 eV, respectively).

knowledge_points.content: Grazing-incident wide-angle X-ray scattering (GIWAXS) reveals that PBDTTS-TTffBT adopts a mixed orientation of face-on and edge-on polymer crystals in the blend, whereas PBDTTS-TTBT takes a predominantly edge-on orientation.
knowledge_points.evidence: This indicates that PBDTTS-TTffBT adopts a mixed orientation of face-on and edge-on while PBDTTS-TTBT takes predominantly the edge-on orientation.

knowledge_points.content: PBDTTS-TTffBT:PC71BM devices exhibit higher and more balanced charge carrier mobilities, with a hole mobility of 6.12 x 10^-4 cm²/Vs and an electron mobility of 5.71 x 10^-4 cm²/Vs.
knowledge_points.evidence: hole mobilities (μh)... PBDTTS-TTffBT:PC71BM blend are... 6.12 x 10-4 cm2 V-1 s-1... electron mobilities (μe)... 5.71 x 10-4 cm2 V-1 s-1

knowledge_points.content: The optimal morphology for PBDTTS-TTffBT and PBDTTS-TTBT solar cells was achieved by using chlorobenzene (CB) as the primary solvent with 1.5 vol% of 1,8-diiodooctane (DIO) as a processing additive.
knowledge_points.evidence: we used a mixed solvent (chlorobenzene (CB) with 1.5 vol% of 1,8-diiodooctane (DIO))

knowledge_points.content: The maximum rate of exciton generation (Gmax) for PBDTTS-TTffBT-based devices is 8.15 x 10^27 m^-3 s^-1, which is approximately 15% higher than that of PBDTTS-TTBT devices (7.09 x 10^27 m^-3 s^-1).
knowledge_points.evidence: The Gmax of PBDTTS-TTffBT-based device is 15% higher than that of the PBDTTS-TTBT-based one... Gmax: 7.09 x 1027 (BT) vs 8.15 x 1027 (ffBT)

knowledge_points.content: Both PBDTTS-TTBT and PBDTTS-TTffBT demonstrate high thermal stability, showing a 5% weight loss temperature at approximately 350 °C.
knowledge_points.evidence: exhibit high thermal stability with 5% weight loss at 350 °C

knowledge_points.content: Resonant soft X-ray scattering (RSoXS) analysis shows that the PBDTTS-TTffBT:PC71BM blend has a characteristic domain size of 33 nm and exhibits higher phase purity compared to the non-fluorinated version.
knowledge_points.evidence: PBDTTS-TTffBT:PC71BM blend shows a distinct shoulder at q = 0.19 nm-1 corresponding to the domain size of 33 nm... PBDTTS-TTffBT:PC71BM BHJ blend is higher than PBDTTS-TTBT:PC71BM blend.

knowledge_points.content: Bimolecular recombination is significantly suppressed in PBDTTS-TTffBT devices, as indicated by a power-law exponent (α) of 0.99 in the relationship between short-circuit current (Jsc) and light intensity (P).
knowledge_points.evidence: Logarithmic plots of Jsc versus P (Figure 3b) show slopes of 0.96 and 0.99 for the devices made of PBDTTS-TTBT:PC71BM and PBDTTS-TTffBT:PC71BM respectively, indicating that the bimolecular recombination in PBDTTS-TTffBT-based device is smaller
